clue.text: School teashop recycling waste here

parts.note: a comp is a comprehensive, the standard British state secondary school

indicators.note: recycling material turns it into something new, so these letters are reworked into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A school is turning its café into a recycling project for food waste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recycling' looks like part of the green scene but is the anagram signal. COMP is short for comprehensive, Britain's standard state secondary school.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden pile where kitchen and garden scraps are left to rot is exactly where waste goes.

clue.text: Bedroom items, perhaps sketched bosoms?

definitions.meaning: pieces of furniture with drawers kept in a bedroom
read whimsically, the chests (bosoms) belonging to people who draw, i.e. artists' subjects

explanation.surface: A list of bedroom furnishings, then a cheeky query about life drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'drawers' as people who draw, so their chests are bosoms that get sketched.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedroom furniture with sliding compartments for clothes is the plain sense; the pun reads chests drawn by artists.

clue.text: Setter affectedly touching fabric

parts.note: the setter is 'me', and the affected, mock-French way to say me is moi
re means concerning or about, i.e. touching on

explanation.surface: The crossword setter is being precious about handling some cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' is the crossword convention for the setter himself, 'me'; said with Miss Piggy affectation it becomes MOI.
explanation.definitionFit: Moiré is a watered silk with a rippling pattern, so it is a kind of textile.

clue.text: One's blown last of moola, air con needing repair

indicators.note: something needing repair is broken, so these letters are to be put back in a new working order
picks the final letter of the word moola

explanation.surface: Someone has spent their last money on an air conditioner that now needs fixing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing repair' rearranges AIR CON to OCARIN; the A ending 'moola' completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument, so it is something a player blows into.

clue.text: Educational opportunity for everyone is canned

indicators.note: something canned is put inside a tin, so the word for everyone goes inside

parts.note: canned goods come in a tin
each, as in a price of five pounds each, means for everyone

explanation.surface: An educational opportunity for all has been cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canned' does double duty: it supplies the TIN and says EACH is put into it. 'Canned' in the surface means scrapped.
explanation.definitionFit: A teach-in is an informal series of lectures and debates on a topical issue, a learning occasion.

clue.text: They add colour to online book

parts.note: E is the standard prefix for electronic or online, as in email
Numbers is the fourth book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: An online book that brightens things up.
explanation.walkthrough: E numbers are the code numbers given to food additives in Europe, many of them colourings.
explanation.definitionFit: Many of these coded food additives are dyes that give processed foods their colour.

clue.text: Average, struggling Inter Milan twice letting in a sitter?

parts.note: par is the normal or average level

indicators.note: a struggling side is in disarray, so these letters are thrown into a new order
says the letter a is used two times

explanation.surface: An average Inter Milan side is struggling and concedes twice to an easy chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' mixes INTER MILAN with A twice ('letting in' joins them) into LIAMENTARIAN. A 'sitter' in football is an easy chance; here it is one who sits in Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A member who sits in the legislature is a sitter there; the query flags that definition by example.

clue.text: Youngster's tucked into cake and salad as a working rule

indicators.note: the youngster is placed inside, between the two foods

parts.note: parkin is a sticky oatmeal and treacle gingerbread from northern England
slaw is short for coleslaw
a son is a youngster; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A child is tucking into cake and salad.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface has the child eating; 'tucked into' instead places the youngster between the foods. Parkin is a Yorkshire treacle cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Parkinson's law, that work expands to fill the time available, is a principle about how jobs behave.

clue.text: Cleaner animals show distress, seized by nurse

indicators.note: something seized is held inside the grasp, so these words go inside the nurse

parts.note: a carer looks after someone, as a nurse does
pets are domestic animals
to weep is to cry, showing distress

explanation.surface: A cleaner's animals are upset after being grabbed by a nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: This manual device with rotating brushes picks up crumbs from rugs, so it is a household cleaning tool.

clue.text: Country crime waves interrupting drivers

indicators.note: the jumbled word breaks into the motoring organisation's letters

parts.note: the AA, Automobile Association, is the British motorists' organisation

indicators.note: waves move things about, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Waves of crime disrupt the nation's motorists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waves' poses as a crime wave but is the anagram signal. The AA is Britain's Automobile Association.
explanation.definitionFit: The United States is commonly called by this name, so it is a nation.

clue.text: Tanks in army's front, as bearing westwards

indicators.note: takes the leading letter of army's

parts.note: qua is Latin for 'in the capacity of', i.e. as

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left

parts.note: air is one's bearing or manner

explanation.surface: Tanks at the front of an army are pointed west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'westwards' turns AIR into RIA. 'Tanks' pretends to be military vehicles but means fish tanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Glass containers for keeping fish are tanks, and aquaria is the Latin plural for them.

clue.text: Between 9 and 11 put on clothing that's playful

indicators.note: one piece is placed after the other, put on to it

parts.note: kit is a set of clothes, as in football kit
a vague time between nine and eleven is about ten, or ten-ish

explanation.surface: Getting dressed some time between nine and eleven, in a playful mood.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers look like cross-references to other clues, but are just times: roughly ten o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaving like a young cat, frisky and full of fun, is being playful.

clue.text: How Brexit begins with hopeless nationalist

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of Brexit

parts.note: limp means feeble or ineffectual

explanation.surface: A comment on how Brexit got off to a weak start, driven by a jingoist.
explanation.walkthrough: Colonel Blimp was a cartoon character, a pompous reactionary jingoist, giving the word for such a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A blimp is a pompous, reactionary, flag-waving patriot, after the cartoon colonel.

clue.text: Unacceptable to lose heart in retreat

indicators.note: the middle letter of the phrase for unacceptable is dropped

parts.note: not OK means unacceptable

explanation.surface: It is wrong to become discouraged during a withdrawal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lose heart' removes the central T from NOT OK.
explanation.definitionFit: A small secluded corner where one can withdraw is a retreat.

clue.text: Note covering wraps round nuts and washer

indicators.note: the note and the covering go around the jumbled letters

parts.note: la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale
a mat is a floor covering

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of round go haywire

explanation.surface: A list from a hardware store: a covering, nuts and a washer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' and 'washer' pose as hardware: 'nuts' is the anagram signal, and the washer is a place that washes clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-service launderette is a place where clothes get washed, cryptically something that washes.

clue.text: Performers with elevated pitch, primarily Italians?

definitions.text: Performers with elevated pitch, primarily Italians?

parts.note: the cast are the performers of a show

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read from the bottom up

parts.note: tar is pitch, the black sticky substance

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of Italians

explanation.surface: High-voiced singers, mostly from Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' turns TAR upwards to RAT. The whole clue also defines: castrated male singers kept high voices and were mainly Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: These were male singers castrated before puberty to keep a soprano or alto range, chiefly in Italian opera.

clue.text: They might produce arts with models

definitions.text: They might produce arts with models

indicators.note: the letters given could be made into something new, rearranged

explanation.surface: Great painters worked with sitters to create their art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might produce' rearranges ARTS and MODELS ('with' joins them). The whole clue also defines: great painters made art using models.
explanation.definitionFit: Great European painters of earlier centuries created artworks, often painting from sitters.

clue.text: Kind of cross about clever dramatic scene

indicators.note: the cross goes around the other word

parts.note: a tau cross is T-shaped
able means skilled or clever

explanation.surface: An irritated person is shrewd about a theatrical moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of cross' looks like a type of anger; it is the T-shaped tau cross.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a striking group or picture, often a frozen staged moment, so it is a theatrical scene.

clue.text: Means to get around bodily pain mostly fake

parts.note: a rick is a sprain or wrench of a joint

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for fake is dropped

parts.note: sham means fake

explanation.surface: A way of dodging physical pain that is mostly faked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the final M from SHAM.
explanation.definitionFit: This two-wheeled hooded cart pulled by a person is a form of transport, a way of travelling.

clue.text: Experienced audio novel

indicators.note: audio means heard, so the word is taken as it sounds

parts.note: novel means new

explanation.surface: An audiobook of a novel that someone has already heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Knew is the past tense of know, and to have known something is to have experienced it.

clue.text: Some characters in Tristram Shandy are flipping clever!

indicators.note: flipping over means reading the run of letters backwards; it also poses as a mild British oath
a few consecutive letters of the title are taken

explanation.surface: Some of the characters in Sterne's novel are flipping clever!
explanation.walkthrough: TRAMS sits in triSTRAM Shandy; 'flipping' turns it round. 'Flipping' as a mild oath is the disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: Being smart means being quick-witted and intelligent, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Rugby player's speed is key

parts.note: a back is a rugby player behind the scrum; the 's is part of the letters
pace is speed

explanation.surface: A rugby player's speed is the key to his game.
explanation.definitionFit: Backspace is a keyboard button that deletes the previous character.

clue.text: Holy man's morning in Westminster?

indicators.note: the time of day is placed inside the district code

parts.note: SW1 is the London postcode of Westminster, written with a one read as I
a.m. means morning

explanation.surface: A holy man's dawn at the centre of British government.
explanation.walkthrough: SW1 is the postcode for Westminster, London's district of Parliament; the 1 is read as letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A swami is a Hindu religious teacher, so a revered spiritual figure.

clue.text: One swallowing tablet and rubbish synthetic material

indicators.note: the first word takes the others inside it

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet
tat is cheap rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone swallowing a pill and some trash, then some fake fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tablet' gives E, slang for an ecstasy pill; 'One' is the ace in cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetate is a man-made fibre or film made from cellulose, so it is an artificial fabric.

clue.text: Covers of sublime track in Beach Boys' territory

indicators.note: takes the outside letters of the word sublime

parts.note: the A-side is the main track of a single

explanation.surface: Cover versions of a sublime track in the style of the Beach Boys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covers' and 'track' look like music talk for the band; they give SE and A-SIDE. The definition is literal: beach boys belong by the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Boys who hang about on the beach are found on the coast, the place by the sea.

clue.text: Model welcomes tip for tantric arousal

indicators.note: the model takes the letter inside it

parts.note: a simulation is a model of a process

indicators.note: takes the first letter of tantric

explanation.surface: A model welcomes advice on tantric sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcomes' puts T, the tip of 'tantric', into SIMULATION after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: Stimulation is excitement or rousing of the senses, as arousal is.
